body.x: LordSystem, led by CEO Jang Yang-ho, appeared at the global media event 'CES Unveiled,' held just before the official opening of CES 2024 on January 7th in Las Vegas. The company, known for developing the 'TripPASS' platform catering to global travelers, is a venture enterprise with Innobiz certification and has developed numerous technologies to prevent information forgery and unauthorized usage, including end-to-end encrypted data transmission and extraction of e-passport chips. Adhering to international financial cloud standards and employing a high-level security system based on blockchain DID, LordSystem has maximized the reliability of its TripPASS service.

LordSystem, recognized by the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) for its nine innovative security technologies, has also secured 35 domestic and international patents related to mobile passports, including in the USA, Japan, China, and the EU, along with achieving the international standard software quality certification (ISO/IEC 25023).

TripPASS goes beyond the convenience of existing payment services, offering a unique feature where a single QR code scan enables simple payments and tax refund services. This innovation in authentication and payment convenience for cross-border travelers is not only transforming tourism services digitally. Still, it is also highly regarded for its potential to expand into mobile tourism financial services and the big data industry.

body.cap: LordSystem representatives are engaging with the international press at the CES Unveiled event. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: LordSystem won the Best Innovation Award in the Financial Technologies category and the Innovation Award in Cybersecurity & Personal Privacy at CES 2024 by showcasing these innovations. CEO Jang Yang-ho expressed his excitement about the global media's interest in their technology, emphasizing the importance of showcasing their capabilities to international media representatives. He further shared his belief in the impact their coverage could have on global markets, reinforcing LordSystem's commitment to leading the mobile passport era.

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), host of CES, the world's largest IT exhibition, provides an annual platform in Las Vegas every January to showcase global consumer electronics trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting on CES news worldwide since 2006, highlighting 'BEST OF CES' and 'BEST OF MADE IN KOREA' in products, companies, and technologies. They also discuss pressing issues from the CES scene through 'AVING LIVE.'

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion, operating on its most enormous scale since Seoul's first CES participation in 2020, is a joint effort of 13 organizations, including SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Campus Town, AI Yangjae Hub, Gwanak District, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, Konkuk University, and Kyung Hee University. This collaborative pavilion marks a significant step in Seoul's ambition to become a startup hub, and among its participating companies, 17 received innovation awards, evidencing their excellence. The pavilion also includes 85 supporters in a significant collaboration between companies, institutions, and industry-academia cooperation.
